Reliability of specimen matrices in a submerged or decomposed body

Source: R/tox.R
mtxrel.Rd

Ranks the specimen matrices of a case (vitreous humour, liver, femoral blood) by how far their results can be trusted. Each matrix starts from a reliability in a fresh body, base, which the user sets from the literature for the analyte at hand; decomposition lowers every matrix by stage / smax, at most by scap, and water dilutes the matrices marked dil (blood, urine) by a further days / dmax, at most dcap. A transparent ordering, not an estimate.

Usage

mtxrel(
  base,
  dil,
  days = 0,
  stage = 0,
  dmax = 30,
  dcap = 0.8,
  smax = 10,
  scap = 0.6
)

Arguments

base

The reliability of each matrix in a fresh body: numbers from 0, named by matrix.

dil

Whether water dilutes each matrix: TRUE or FALSE, one per matrix.

days

The days the body was submerged: one number from 0.

stage

The decomposition stage (0 fresh): one number from 0.

dmax, smax

The days and the stage at which the loss reaches its rate's full scale: positive numbers.

dcap, scap

The largest losses to dilution and to decomposition: numbers from 0 to 1.

Value

A data frame with one row per matrix, the most reliable first: matrix (the names of base, or their numbers), base, rel the reliability after the losses, dil, rank.

References

Dinis-Oliveira, R. J., Carvalho, F., Duarte, J. A., Remiao, F., Marques, A., Santos, A. and Magalhaes, T. (2010). Collection of biological samples in forensic toxicology. Toxicology Mechanisms and Methods, 20(7), 363-414. doi:10.3109/15376516.2010.497976

Examples

base <- c(vitreous = 0.95, liver = 0.8, femoral = 0.55, heart = 0.35)
mtxrel(base, dil = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE), days = 12, stage = 3)
#>     matrix base   rel   dil rank
#> 1 vitreous 0.95 0.665 FALSE    1
#> 2    liver 0.80 0.560 FALSE    2
#> 3  femoral 0.55 0.231  TRUE    3
#> 4    heart 0.35 0.147  TRUE    4
